Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates asymmetry of the pulmonary vasculature with a diminutive right hilum and decreased vascular markings in the right lung, which are classic radiographic signs of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or hypoplasia associated with Takayasu arteritis. This is corroborated by the axial CT image (Figure 2b), which shows calcification and narrowing of the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), confirming a chronic stenotic process rather than an acute embolic event or bilateral disease.
